chunk_findings.detail: `_ci_partial_here` omits the `tree is None` guard that its sibling `_ci_baseline_red` explicitly has. Given an item whose `ci` gate has `outcome="partial"` and `evidence={"tree_sha": "<sha>+clean"}` but whose current tree/worktree is `None`, `red = _ci_baseline_red(it, tree) or _ci_partial_here(it, tree)` first calls `_ci_baseline_red`, which returns `False` because the outcome is not `"red"`, then calls `_ci_partial_here`. With a non-empty clean evidence fingerprint, `_ci_partial_here` evaluates `G.normal_fingerprint(G.tree_identity(tree))` with `tree=None`. The sibling helper’s `tree is None or ...` guard indicates `tree_identity` is not expected to accept `None`; this should return `False` and let `unit_tests` still require CI, but instead it can raise an exception and break the gate.

chunk_findings.detail: If a person-only baseline-red partial has no recorded `baseline.auto.why` evidence, the new code still produces the original silent refusal. For example, given `GateRecord("unit_tests", "partial", ..., {"baseline": {"red": True}})` (the plausible “automatic path is off by default” case from the bug description), `why_not_accepted` returns `{"unit_tests": ""}`, so `reasons` is empty and the refusal message omits any explanation. Thus the change does not actually tell the operator whether the automatic path was disabled or its conditions were unmet; it only helps when the gate run already recorded a non-empty reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/merge_force.py:why_not_accepted / refusal

chunk_findings.detail: This is not a regression test for the reported merge path. It calls `MF.why_not_accepted` directly and injects the result into an `Assessment`, so it can pass even if the production `assess()` path fails to populate `why`. For instance, if `assess()` returned `why={}` despite the same evidence, `ddflow merge` would still refuse silently, but this test would still pass because it bypasses `assess()`. It also has no case for missing/empty `baseline.auto.why`, which is exactly the remaining silent-refusal behavior described above.

chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback does not actually identify the missing automatic-acceptance reason; it substitutes an unevidenced guess that can be false. `why_not_accepted` returns `NO_REASON` whenever `baseline.auto.why` is absent, without consulting `[gates].baseline_red_auto`, the measurement time, or the baseline-red auto-accept conditions. Given a current gate run made while the automatic path is enabled, with evidence such as `{"baseline": {"red": True}}` but no `baseline.auto.why` (the reported “conditions ... not met silently” case), `assess()` produces `why={"unit_tests": NO_REASON}` and `refusal()` says “Not accepted automatically because unit_tests: [gates].baseline_red_auto is off or the measurement predates it.” In that input both parts of the disjunction are false: the automatic path is not off and the measurement does not predate it.
